Use case: stylized-concept. D — true 2D PIXEL ART asset sheet, a gridded roster for a 1990s handheld arcade arena game. Each enemy looks like a real 48×48 or 64×64 top-down 16-bit sprite drawn one pixel at a time and enlarged 4× by nearest-neighbor. Big uniform square pixels; stair-step contours; hand-clustered hard-edged highlights and small checkerboard dithering; few colors per sprite. Deep navy field with thin muted-blue grid. Electric fuchsia, cyan, gold, teal, violet and coral role accents. Strong high three-quarter view, visible upper silhouettes and mostly compact footprints. Distinct sprite forms: one-eyed tracked crab, sharp jet-shaped runner, square punching power loader, coil gunner, spear bug, spherical battery walker, blinking repair drone. Boss fills its cell as a bold 16-bit purple siege crawler with a luminous center. No 3D lighting, bevels, realistic textures, vector curves, bloom, blur, gradients or smooth edges. Design the number labels as crisp arcade bitmap lettering.

Exactly 15 numbered enemy designs in a 3-column × 5-row portrait roster, in this order. A small clear cell number is the only text, no titles or decoration. Row 1: 01 basic small ground melee pursuer, 02 ultra-light fast scout, 03 wide heavy melee with blunt fists and no cannon. Row 2: 04 shooter with a short forward blaster, 05 low charger with two ramming prongs, 06 bomber with a caged spherical payload. Row 3: 07 repair unit with a clear plus and tool arm, 08 splitter with two interlocking halves and a bright center seam, 09 summoner with two deployment hatches. Row 4: 10 sniper with a long precision barrel, 11 mortar with an upward tube and stable legs, 12 teleporter with a broken ring and core. Row 5: 13 tall signal booster with radial fins, 14 armored enemy with broad frontal shield, 15 arena boss with a low body, many heavy legs and exposed top reactor. Full forms inside their cells with clear space, no overlaps. Keep details legible at small mobile game size. 1024×1536 portrait composition. Invent shapes and palettes for this medium, without referencing any existing designs, games or franchises.

Use case: stylized-concept. E — DRAWN INK COMIC concept sheet for a top-down action game, stark two-color indie graphic novel / screenprint look. Real pen-and-brush work on warm off-white paper, deep cobalt near-black ink, strong bold dark outer contours, confident dry-brush accents and graphic flat shadows with deliberately limited burnt-orange spot color for power and role signs. Mostly flat drawn 2D shapes and dramatic caricature proportions, irregular sketchlike lines, visible coarse cross-hatching where needed, asymmetry and animated gestures. Show elevated front three-quarter view. The faction is living mechanical relics shaped like antique forged masks, insect harnesses, iron bells and old knight armor; tell roles through anatomy. 01 is a tiny iron mask with thin talons, 03 a mountain of linked hammer plates, 07 an inlaid plus on an old medical satchel, 15 a monstrously broad armored stag beetle with orange ring reactor. Grid drawn in fine ink with restrained gutters. Small hand-lettered numbers. No CGI shading, no polished enamel, no detailed realistic render, no gradient, no anime faces, no background scenery. It must immediately read as a hand-drawn comic book printed on paper.

Use case: stylized-concept. F — HANDMADE PLASTICINE STOP-MOTION toys photographed from an elevated front angle on lilac studio paper. Soft round pinched shapes with thumbprints, slightly imperfect clay seams, handmade shapes, a cheerful toybox aesthetic and bold silhouette variations. Tactile matte material. Bold candy palettes per role: lemon yellow, raspberry pink, sky blue, tangerine, mint and grape, with round button eyes, molded surface dots and very simple joint construction. Clean art-directed miniature photography, real broad soft ground-contact shadows and consistent illumination. This is whimsical toy fabrication: round jellybean walkers, spring feet, tubby rounded tanks, bead-and-noodle mechanisms, striped clay balls and a giant rounded boss with a bright inset reactor like a swirl of clay. Weapons are simple chunky colored clay shapes and legible. No sharp polygons, rust, ink outlines, realistic sci-fi panels, intricate greebles, neon edge lighting, or metallic glints. Uniform simple pastel grid and small dark readable numbers. Clearly distinct from both pixel art and graphic novel illustration.
